Collection/Nero Marquina
N° 02 / 08

nero marquina

[ 01 ] — Character

Deep black, struck through with white calcite. Few stones draw a sharper line.

Nero Marquina comes from the hills around Markina, in the Basque Country of northern Spain. It is a fine-grained black stone crossed by irregular white veins. Polished, it turns almost mirror-black; honed, it softens toward charcoal.

Origin
Markina, Basque Country, Spain
Stone
Marble
Ground
Deep, even black
Veining
Sharp white calcite, bold to hair-fine
Finishes
Polished, honed, brushed, bush-hammered
Formats
Slabs, tiles, cut-to-size

[ 04 ] — Laying it out

Open the block like a book.

Slabs sawn one after another from the same block carry the same vein. How they are laid decides the drawing on the wall.

[ 05 ] — Where it works

Rooms it was made for.

  • 01

    Chequerboard floors

    The classic partner to white marble, tile against tile.

  • 02

    Bathrooms

    Vanity tops, basin surrounds and wall cladding.

  • 03

    Worktops and bars

    Seal it: acids leave pale marks, and they show on black.

  • 04

    Feature walls

    Book-matched, the white veins join into one figure.

  • 05

    Stairs and thresholds

    Honed or brushed, for grip and a softer black.

  • 06

    Tables and plinths

    A dark base that makes whatever stands on it stand out.
